Transcript:
[00:00] Jasper Lee: hey everyone thanks for being here, uh we wanted to keep this pretty focused, i'm jasper from redwood inference, i'm the account lead. rina is our systems engineer and noah is our success manager. good to meet you all.
[00:12] Miguel Santos: hey jasper thanks. quick note we're on east-coast, so apologies for the early time for some of the team.
[00:18] Priya Nair: thanks, yeah we have a short agenda, mainly want to confirm network & security constraints so we can start the pilot.
[00:24] Rina Patel: great, i can take the network piece. before we dive, could you give a one-line on what you're aiming to validate in the pilot? like throughput vs latency vs cost tradeoff?
[00:34] Priya Nair: sure. primary is latency for user-facing embeddings and chat features in our customer console, second is cost — we need to prove we can be sub-$0.01 per 1k tokens equivalent with batching, and third is data isolation so no customer PII leaves our VPC.
[00:50] Jasper Lee: perfect, that's actually aligned with what we see: low-latency interactive traffic, with occasional bulk embedding jobs. for the pilot we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated — reserved capacity with a small GPU pool — to get predictable latencies and isolated networking.
[01:05] Ethan Cole: when you say reserved capacity, are we talking about dedicated instances in our VPC or redwood-managed infra with peering? security wants to know if keys ever touch a third party.
[01:18] Noah Kim: good question — for Dedicated we offer two flavours: a hosted-dedicated where hardware is logically isolated in our infra but redwood handles the machines, and Private where we deploy into your VPC (VPC peering or customer-managed infra). for a first pilot most customers do hosted-dedicated + peering if they want to keep traffic over a private link; we can also do a full private deployment if you need on-prem.
[01:40] Samir Rao: our compliance bar: SOC2 in place, and we need KMS integration so keys never leave our tenant. we also need audit logs exported to our SIEM. can you confirm those options?
[01:52] Rina Patel: yes, we support customer-managed KMS (K-M-S) integration and HSM flows for Private deployments; audit logs can be forwarded to S3 or your SIEM via syslog / secure forwarder. i will attach the doc after this call. note: sometimes the auto-transcripts say K V cache instead of KMS — ignore that, that's the STT artifact.
[02:10] Lina Park: any constraints on egress for the models? we have tight egress budgeting.
[02:15] Jasper Lee: the runtime itself doesn't require outbound egress except for control plane health checks; model artifacts can be pinned in your region and we can avoid pull-through by pre-staging the weights. for our hosted-dedicated pilot we recommend pre-staging to reduce egress.
[02:28] Miguel Santos: ok good. priya, what models are we testing?
[02:31] Priya Nair: two sizes: a smaller 7B variant for embeddings and quick chat completion, and a 70B-ish model for higher-quality summarization. we also want to try 4-bit quantized variants to check perf/cost.
[02:45] Rina Patel: that aligns. worth noting that quantization changes perf characteristics; we can run a small bench with continuous-batch settings and KV-cache warmups. would you be able to share a representative prompt set and sequence length distribution?
[02:59] Priya Nair: yes i'll drop a sample set after the call.
[03:03] Ethan Cole: network specifics — we use private subnets with restricted NAT, and we have a NAT gateway only for outbound. our security team prefers VPC peering over internet egress.
[03:12] Jasper Lee: VPC peering is supported, and we also have private-link style options. i'll send the peering template.
[03:18] Samir Rao: on SSO: we use SAML + SCIM for provisioning. support for role-based access control (RBAC) is required.
[03:25] Noah Kim: yep full SAML SSO, SCIM, and RBAC roles are supported in the console. we can map your IdP groups to project/route-level access.
[03:33] Miguel Santos: can you clarify observability — we need per-route latency and token-level cost breakdowns, and traces that map back to our request IDs.
[03:43] Rina Patel: redwood console provides per-model and per-route dashboards, spans and traces — though the trace naming may have some small differences, sometimes the auto-agent labels models as 'redwood-ded' in our internals, the UI will show the full model name. We can also expose request-id headers so your tracing ingests line up.
[04:02] Priya Nair: perfect. in terms of timeline, we want pilot running in 2 weeks and production in 10 weeks — is that realistic?
[04:12] Jasper Lee: two weeks for pilot is tight but feasible if network artifacts are ready. the critical path is VPC peering and KMS proofs; we'll need your firewall rules and a peering CIDR by next tuesday (2026-02-06).
[04:25] Ethan Cole: acknowledged. i'll compile the CIDR and firewall list, but we might need help mapping ports.
[04:30] Rina Patel: i'll include a minimal port list in the peering template; generally we need control plane ports, and an internal TLS port for the runtime.
[04:40] Miguel Santos: for billing — do you pro-rate or have minimums for dedicated? we want limited spend during pilot.
[04:47] Jasper Lee: pilot pricing we typically offer a 4-week pilot credit and a short-term reserved pool at a reduced rate; i'll send a pilot SOW with numbers. for longer-term we can discuss commit discounts.
[04:58] Priya Nair: for the perf bench, can you run both p99 latency and median with our prompt set plus concurrency that matches a 100-reqs/min baseline?
[05:09] Rina Patel: yes we'll run bench with target concurrency and include p50/p95/p99, throughput, and token-cost breakdown. note — the p99 can vary a bit on cold starts so we advise warmup runs with KV-cache.
[05:23] Lina Park: on data residency — some EU customers require data not leave eu-west-1. do you have region pinning?
[05:29] Jasper Lee: yes, region pinning is supported for hosted-dedicated and private deployments. we'll map to your requested region and pre-stage models there.
[05:38] Miguel Santos: any gotchas about model licensing? we're using an open model but will want to know what your responsibilities are for hosting weights.
[05:45] Noah Kim: we host customer-specified model binaries; licensing stays with you — we provide the runtime. for some models we maintain certified variants; we'll flag if licensing restricts certain deployments.
[05:57] Priya Nair: ok great. small question on fallback: if Dedicated capacity can't handle spikes, what's the policy? auto-scale? fallback to hosted?
[06:07] Jasper Lee: we have configurable fallbacks — canary, A/B, and region fallback. for Dedicated you can configure burst to hosted capacity or to a secondary model variant. we'll walk through that in the runbook.
[06:20] Miguel Santos: helpful. one more security note: our auditors ask for tamper-evident logs and 90-day retention. can you do that?
[06:29] Rina Patel: retention windows can be configured per-customer and we support immutable storage options with object lock for an audit trail. we'll include the retention options in the security pack.
[06:40] Jasper Lee: okay wrapping into next steps — i'll recap: redwood will send peering template + minimal ports, pilot SOW with pricing, and the security pack (KMS + audit logs + SOC2 artifacts). rina will run a perf pass once priya shares prompts. ethan will send network CIDR and firewall rules.
[06:55] Priya Nair: yep i'll share prompt set and evaluation metrics. is there a test harness you prefer?
[07:01] Rina Patel: we can consume a CSV with input prompts and expected outputs; we also have a simple harness (python) we'll share. sometimes transcripts mislabel the harness name as "harness-lite", it's actually 'redwood-bench' in the repo.
[07:15] Miguel Santos: timeframe again — the team expects pilot live by 2026-02-18, production by end of april.
[07:23] Jasper Lee: pilot by 2/18 is OK as long as the network artifacts are in by 2/6 and we've run the perf bench week-of 2/9. production timeline we'll firm up after pilot results.
[07:35] Ethan Cole: any special compliance docs we should pull ahead of the pilot? SOC2 report, vulnerability scan summary?
[07:41] Noah Kim: we'll share SOC2, pen-test summary redacted, and our security whitepaper. note that the SOC2 is third-party attestation from last quarter.
[07:50] Samir Rao: will you accept our JML (just-in-time) provisioning for SSO? we'd prefer to not provision service accounts until the pilot.
[07:58] Rina Patel: yes, SAML with JIT provisioning is supported; we can treat the initial accounts as limited roles and escalate via SCIM later.
[08:07] Jasper Lee: cool. i'm going to read back the action items then we'll open the floor.
[08:12] Jasper Lee: readback: 1) Ethan to send CIDR/firewall by 2026-02-06; 2) Priya to share prompt set and metrics by 2026-02-05; 3) Rina will run bench and share artifacts by 2026-02-09; 4) Jasper to send pilot SOW, pricing and peering template by 2026-02-05; 5) Redwood to share SOC2 and security pack by 2026-02-05. any edits?
[08:33] Miguel Santos: that's accurate. add: include a short runbook for failure modes on spike handling.
[08:40] Jasper Lee: good call, added.
[08:42] Priya Nair: one minor thing — can the bench include throughput at different token lengths? we typically vary from 64 to 1024 tokens.
[08:50] Rina Patel: yes will include distribution and a per-length breakdown.
[08:54] Jasper Lee: thanks everyone. quick note on comms: we'll create a shared channel and include the runbook and SOW drafts. we'll also schedule the technical deep dive for 2026-02-11 at 15:00 UTC — is that okay?
[09:07] Miguel Santos: that works.
[09:09] Ethan Cole: ok. thanks all.
